findings.detail: `fetchYallaMenu(yalla, targetUrl, (u, init) => fetch(u, init))` keeps a literal `fetch(` token inside `components/`, which is the pattern `handbooks/architecture/frontend-boundaries.md` § rule 2 flags. I am deliberately NOT treating this as a rule-2 violation (hence non-blocking): the thing rule 2 exists to prevent — endpoint choice, headers, concurrency, timeouts living in the component — is exactly what this PR moved into `services/yallaMenuService.ts`, and the injected argument is a test seam, not I/O policy. It is still worth removing so the next reader does not read it as precedent for the surrounding legacy `fetch` calls at lines 83–135.
findings.summary: Component still names `fetch` to inject it into the service

findings.detail: `categories as YallaCategory[]` and `items as YallaItem[]` are asserted after a check that only proves the values are non-empty arrays — nothing validates the elements. If the platform ever returns `[null, …]` or `[{…}, "x"]` in `data`, `live()` at `utils/yallaMenu.ts:51` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'is_deleted')`. I confirmed the blast radius is contained: the throw escapes `fetchYallaMenu` (the `finally` only clears the timer) into the component's `catch` at `components/WebScraperTab.tsx:62`, so the user gets the page-text fallback and a warning rather than a crash. That containment is why this is low rather than medium — without the caller's try/catch it would be a user-facing failure. `handbooks/language/typescript/type-safety.md` § rule 4 is the relevant rule: external data is `unknown` until validated.
findings.summary: `Array.isArray` guard does not justify the element-shape assertion

findings.detail: Each unknown `category` id gets its own synthetic category, all named `(no section)`. With more than one id missing from `/api/categories/`, the output contains repeated `## (no section)` blocks. The items are still all present — the fix in cb2adf7 (never drop an item) holds — so this is cosmetic in the text the model receives, not a data-loss path. Noting it only because the unit test at `tests/unit/yallaMenu.test.ts` covers the single-orphan case and would not catch the duplication if someone later relied on the heading being unique.
findings.summary: Two orphan sections emit two identical `## (no section)` headings
